title: Path A — Foundations
subtitle: Network Protocols, Linux Terminal Mastery, Core Security & Python Automation
description: The mandatory baseline for all cybersecurity specializations. Master TCP/IP networking, Linux terminal operations, core security theory, and defensive Python scripting.

steps.title: Networking Fundamentals
steps.goal: Understand how computers route packets, negotiate handshakes, resolve domains, and segment subnets.
steps.resourceChoice: Select either Jeremy's IT Lab (thorough, with Packet Tracer) or NetworkChuck (faster-paced). You do not need to follow both.
checklist: Explain the OSI 7-layer model and TCP/IP stack mapping
Calculate IPv4 subnet masks and CIDR prefixes (/24, /26, /30)
Describe the TCP three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK)
Inspect DNS lookups and DHCP address leasing
Identify common port numbers (22, 53, 80, 443, 445, 3389)

steps.title: Linux Terminal Fundamentals
steps.goal: Gain comfort navigating the Linux filesystem, editing config files, and piping commands.
checklist: Navigate folders, create, move, and edit text files with nano or vim
Use pipes (|), grep, cut, awk, and sort to filter log files
Understand absolute and relative paths

steps.title: Linux Permissions & Process Management
steps.goal: Master permissions, user management, and service operations for security environments.
checklist: Modify permissions with chmod (octal and symbolic) and chown
Inspect running processes with ps, top, and kill
Manage system services with systemctl (start, status, enable)
Complete OverTheWire Bandit levels 0 to 10

steps.title: Core Security Principles
steps.goal: Internalize defense fundamentals before learning offensive exploitation techniques.
checklist: Explain the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability)
Differentiate authentication vs authorization
Explain Defense-in-Depth, least privilege, and zero trust models

steps.title: Python Scripting for Security
steps.goal: Build small automated utility scripts for hash verification, socket probing, and log parsing.
checklist: Write Python scripts using functions, loops, dictionaries, and file I/O
Create a hash verifier using hashlib (MD5, SHA-256)
Build a basic TCP banner-grabber using the socket library
Parse an Apache or Nginx access log to identify 404/500 anomaly bursts

title: Path B — Security+ Certification Track
subtitle: CompTIA SY0-701 Exam Objectives & Practical Cryptography
description: Structured preparation for the industry-standard entry-level certification. Covers threat vectors, security architecture, risk management, and cryptographic primitives.
prerequisites: Completion of Path A Foundations or equivalent knowledge
versionNotice: This course covers exam SY0-701. The English SY0-701 exam retires on 11 June 2027. The new SY0-801 exam launches around 17 Nov 2026. Check CompTIA's official page for the latest.

steps.title: CompTIA SY0-701 Comprehensive Preparation
steps.goal: Master the 5 core domains of Security+ (General Security Concepts, Threats & Vulnerabilities, Security Architecture, Security Operations, Security Program Management).
checklist: Identify social engineering tactics (phishing, vishing, pretexting)
Compare symmetric vs asymmetric cryptography implementations
Describe network security appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS, proxies)
Understand incident response lifecycle phases
Score 85%+ on full-length domain practice quizzes

steps.title: Deep-Dive Cryptography & Security Mechanisms
steps.goal: Develop an intuitive grasp of mathematical security principles, ciphers, hashing, and key exchange.
checklist: Explain the difference between encoding, encryption, and hashing
Describe RSA public/private key pairs and Diffie-Hellman key exchange
Explain how TLS handshakes establish forward secrecy
Identify hashing collision vulnerabilities (MD5, SHA-1 vs SHA-256)

title: Path C — Ethical Hacking & Practical Pentesting
subtitle: Network Penetration Testing, CTFs & Methodology
description: Learn hands-on offensive security methodologies, reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation, and CTF challenge solving strictly within authorized lab environments.
prerequisites: Basic TCP/IP and Linux command fluency
legalReminder: Strict Legal Rule: Only test systems you own or have explicit, prior written permission to test. Never target unauthorized third-party infrastructure. All skills must be applied solely within designated lab environments or authorized engagements.

steps.title: Practical Network Penetration Testing
steps.goal: Execute end-to-end authorized penetration tests following standard methodology.
checklist: Perform passive and active information gathering
Scan and enumerate open ports with Nmap without alerting rate-limiters
Identify vulnerable software versions against public CVE databases
Safely execute basic exploits in local lab VMs
Document findings with reproduction steps and executive remediation guidance

steps.title: PicoCTF Hands-on Problem Solving
steps.goal: Develop critical thinking and reverse-engineering instincts through guided beginner challenges.
checklist: Solve binary exploitation, web exploitation, and cryptography rooms
Try solving each challenge independently before viewing walkthroughs
Maintain personal technical writeups explaining the root cause of every vulnerability

steps.title: Hack The Box Easy Linux Targets
steps.goal: Transition to realistic target systems featuring complex multi-step attack chains.
checklist: Enumerate web services and local cron jobs on target Linux hosts
Establish initial shell access and upgrade to interactive TTY
Perform Linux local privilege escalation using SUID binaries and sudo privileges
Capture user and root flags legitimately

title: Path D — Web Application Security
subtitle: OWASP Top 10, PortSwigger Web Security Academy & Vulnerable Web Labs
description: Lab-first curriculum focused on detecting and mitigating vulnerabilities in modern web applications, APIs, and client-server architectures.
prerequisites: Familiarity with HTML, JavaScript, and SQL syntax

steps.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy Core Labs
steps.goal: Hands-on mastery of high-impact web vulnerabilities in an enterprise-grade simulator.
checklist: Execute SQL Injection: UNION attacks, error-based, and blind time-delay attacks
Identify and exploit Cross-Site Scripting (Reflected, Stored, and DOM XSS)
Bypass broken authentication mechanisms and test JWT signing flaws
Test for Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR / BOLA)
Inspect Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) access to metadata endpoints

steps.title: Local Vulnerable Apps: OWASP Juice Shop & DVWA
steps.goal: Deploy and test web attack vectors against full-featured modern SPA and classic PHP architectures.
checklist: Spin up OWASP Juice Shop via Docker or Node.js locally
Configure Burp Suite Community Edition proxy and CA certificate
Intercept and manipulate HTTP requests, headers, and JSON payloads
Complete low-to-medium difficulty challenges on DVWA

steps.title: Web Application Pentesting Methodologies
steps.goal: Structured web testing workflow using industry command-line tooling.
steps.specialNote: HackerSploit channel inactive since 2025. Verify commands against current tool documentation.
checklist: Enumerate subdomains and web directories using dirsearch/gobuster
Inspect API endpoints for improper authorization checks
Understand secure coding practices and WAF mitigation techniques

title: Path E — Emerging Tracks (Coming Soon)
subtitle: Specialized Cybersecurity Tracks in Active Development
description: We are curating and independently verifying top-tier free playlists for specialized domains. No unverified URLs are published.

tracks.title: SOC / SIEM / Incident Response (Blue Team)
tracks.summary: Log analysis, SIEM event correlation (Splunk, Elastic), triage, memory forensics, and threat hunting.

tracks.title: Cloud Security (AWS, Azure & GCP)
tracks.summary: Cloud IAM permission boundaries, S3 bucket exposure, Terraform posture management, and container isolation.

tracks.title: AI & LLM Security
tracks.summary: Prompt injection, indirect prompt tampering, insecure output handling, model theft, and RAG data exfiltration.

tracks.title: Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC)
tracks.summary: ISO 27001 controls, NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF 2.0), SOC 2 compliance, and vendor risk assessments.
